text: Man 34 years, watery stool since yesterday, vomiting, no fever, sunken eyes
rationale: Proposed by the reviewer as 'ch-07 (Bauchi)'; renamed ch-12 to avoid an ID collision with our own committed ch-07 (a different case: Lagos, sunken eyes + slow skin pinch, testing the two-of-four dehydration rule in isolation). Sunken eyes plus vomiting in a cholera-prone state. NCDC (guide p.61-62): frequent severe vomiting needs IV therapy, and suspected cases are isolated even without laboratory results. Start ORS, notify the DSNO.
tricky: Only one of the four severe-dehydration signs (sunken eyes); tests the new sunken-eyes-plus-vomiting rule, not the two-of-four rule.

text: Man 30 years, watery stool since yesterday, no vomiting, sunken eyes noted, drinking well, alert
rationale: One sign without vomiting. NCDC (guide p.59-60): Plan B needs a treatment centre or unit with monitoring; refer within 24h and reassess hourly meanwhile.

text: Baby 6 weeks old, hot body since this morning, feeding a little less
rationale: IMCI: any fever in an infant under 2 months.

text: Woman 27 years, 5 months pregnant, fever 2 days, RDT positive, eating and drinking well
rationale: NMEP: adult-dose artemether-lumefantrine (the only ACT recommended in the first trimester). Review at 48 hours and link to antenatal care; refer for any danger sign or Lassa-suggestive feature.

text: Man 30 years, fever 3 days, vomiting once, RDT positive, no sore throat, no contact, no ACT yet
rationale: RDT-positive, high-burden state, no Lassa-suggestive feature: start ACT, standard precautions, upgrade if not better in 48 hours.

text: Woman 29 years, nursed a neighbour who died of a bleeding fever 8 days ago, fever 3 days, vomiting
rationale: Contact within 21 days, any state. Isolate and notify.

text: Doctor 36 years, works in the maternity ward, fever 2 days, headache, RDT positive
rationale: Healthcare worker in a high-burden state in season: report to the DSNO and test; Refer now if exposure to a suspected case is known.

text: Woman 24 years, 30 weeks pregnant, fever 3 days, vomiting, RDT negative
rationale: Pregnancy raises the risk of severe disease and fetal loss.

text: Man 40 years, fever 3 days, RDT positive, breathing 34 per minute and deep
rationale: Adult respiratory rate 30 or more.

text: Pikin 2 years, hot body 1 day, RDT positive, e no dey convulse, e dey play and drink well
rationale: Negation test: the child does not convulse and must not be referred.

text: Pikin 2 years, hot body 2 days, e no fit drink water
rationale: Negation test: "no fit" means cannot.

text: Girl 16 years, 50 kg, fever 2 days, RDT positive, drinking well, last period 10 weeks ago
rationale: Artemether-lumefantrine 4 tablets x 6 doses (NMEP: ACTs are recommended in the first trimester). Advise a pregnancy test and review at 2 days.

text: Girl 5 years, 18 kg, RDT positive, vomited the first artemether-lumefantrine dose after 15 minutes, repeated it and vomited again
rationale: NMEP: repeat once if vomiting within 30 minutes; a second vomit needs a parenteral antimalarial, so refer. Dose would have been 2 tablets.

text: Girl 13 years, 35.0 kg, fever 2 days, RDT positive, drinking well
rationale: 4 tablets x 6 doses (WHO 35 kg or more). NMEP prints 25 to under 35 and over 35 kg, leaving exactly 35.0 kg unassigned; query NMEP.

text: Boy 18 months, watery stools since morning, restless and irritable, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly
rationale: NCDC chart: 2 or more moderate signs = Plan B in a treatment centre (ORS 75 mL per kg over 4 hours; 600 to 800 mL at this age if weight unknown). At 18 months he is below the IDSR cholera case-definition age of 2 years, so manage as acute watery diarrhoea with dehydration (IMCI and NCDC plans); referral is the same. Upgrade if repeated vomiting.

text: Man 38 years, fever 4 days, now confused and drowsy, RDT positive, neck stiff
rationale: Parasitaemia can be incidental to coma, and a stiff neck keeps meningitis first. First dose of a parenteral antibiotic before transfer where available and trained.

text: Man 40 years, bleeding gums and nosebleeds for 2 days, no fever, no injury, no known bleeding disorder
rationale: IDSR: any person with inexplicable bleeding is a suspected Lassa case; fever is not required. Isolate and notify.

text: Baby 9 months, hot body since yesterday, one convulsion, now alert and feeding, neck not stiff
rationale: NCDC 2023 infant definition lists fever with convulsion; also an IMCI danger sign. Do not assume a febrile seizure. First-dose antibiotic before transfer where trained.

text: Man 22 years, fever 2 days, severe headache, cannot look at bright light, neck stiff
rationale: Osun is one of the southern states NCDC lists inside the meningitis belt (with Bayelsa, Cross River, Delta, Ekiti, Ogun, Ondo). The rule must not depend on a northern state. Photophobia plus neck stiffness: refer.

text: Man 34 years, watery stool since yesterday, vomiting, no fever, sunken eyes
rationale: The live case from the logic review, in a state the supplied yaml removed from the cholera list although Kano appears in the 2021, 2023 and 2026 NCDC reports (13 cases and 1 death in 2024). The two-of-four rule alone would not fire (one sign); the sunken-eyes-plus-vomiting rule must, and must not depend on the baseline list.

text: Man 35 years, fever 5 days, sore throat, vomiting, RDT negative, took artemether-lumefantrine with no change
rationale: Kogi is a reported (not high-burden) Lassa state in the supplied yaml, which gives no escalation on its own. NCDC case definition met plus failed treatment: needs the any-state floor.

text: Child 3 years, cough 2 days, breathing fast, no chest indrawing, drinking well, playful, RDT negative
rationale: IMCI: fast breathing alone is pneumonia, not a danger sign. The logic review excludes fast breathing alone, but its respiratory-distress phrase list appears to include "fast breathing"; this case tests that.

text: Girl 15 years, fever 2 days, RDT positive, says she is bleeding from her period
rationale: Menstrual bleeding is not abnormal bleeding. The bleeding rule (blood from the vagina) would force Refer now; ask about the cause first. Record pregnancy status.

text: Woman 28 years, profuse watery stools since morning, vomited twice, very thirsty, restless, eyes look sunken
rationale: Three moderate signs (restless, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly) = Plan B, which NCDC and the IDSR say needs a treatment centre or unit; with vomiting in a state the yaml dropped but which was second in NCDC's 2024 report (64 cases), many services would treat this as Refer now.
